items.title: Ruto’s Sh5tn transformation plan: What has Kenya achieved one year on?
items.description: President William Ruto returns to Parliament a year after unveiling a Sh5 trillion economic transformation plan.
content: NAIROBI, Kenya, Nov 18 —President William Ruto returns to Parliament on Wednesday for his 2026 State of the Nation Address facing scrutiny over the implementation of a Sh5 trillion transformation blueprint he unveiled nearly a year ago, promising to reposition Kenya as a competitive, industrialised and export-oriented economy.

The annual address is a constitutional requirement under Article 132(1)(c), which obligates the President to report to Parliament on measures taken and progress achieved in the realisation of national values set out under Article 10 of the Constitution.

In his November 20, 2025 State of the Nation Address, Ruto outlined four priorities: investing in people, transforming Kenya into a net exporter, expanding water storage and irrigation, and upgrading energy generation and transport infrastructure.

The President estimated that the programme would require at least Sh5 trillion over a decade, proposing a National Infrastructure Fund (NIF) and a Sovereign Wealth Fund (SWF) to mobilise capital without relying excessively on public borrowing.

The blueprint included targets to construct at least fifty mega dams, bring 2.5 million acres under irrigation, add 10,000 megawatts to electricity generation capacity and tarmac 28,000 kilometres of roads.

The United Nations has opened applications for its 2026 Young Professionals Programme (YPP), offering entry-level professional positions in Development and Sustainability at the P-1 and P-2 grades across several UN duty stations, including Nairobi.
The application deadline is 30 November 2026 at 11:59 p.m. New York time.
The YPP is the UN Secretariat's primary recruitment pathway for early-career professionals seeking to serve as international civil servants.

The programme combines an entrance examination with structured professional development and is open exclusively to nationals of countries that are unrepresented or under-represented within the Secretariat.

The list of eligible countries shifts each year.
Five African nations are included in the 2026 cycle: Angola, Equatorial Guinea, Liberia, Libya, and São Tomé and Príncipe.

Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa , and Ethiopia do not appear on the list, making their nationals ineligible to apply through the standard nationality-based route this year.

Kenyans who hold dual nationality with one of the qualifying countries may still be considered, provided they enter that nationality in the "Country of Nationality" field and attach a government-issued photo ID confirming it.
The UN has clarified that nationality at birth and other secondary nationalities are not taken into account for YPP eligibility.

To qualify, candidates must be nationals of a participating Member State, hold at least a bachelor's degree in a relevant field, be 32 years old or younger during the examination year, meaning born on or after January 1, 1994, and demonstrate proficiency in English or French at UN Level II or above.

Prior work experience is not mandatory, though it may be used to rank applicants when large volumes of applications are received from a single country.
The 2026 examination covers economics, statistics, social affairs, environmental issues, sustainable development, technology and digital transformation, and programme management support.
Assessment proceeds in three stages: application screening, a written examination, and an oral interview.
The written exam is split into two parts, with Part I tentatively scheduled for February 2027 and the oral stage anticipated for mid-2027.
Candidates placed on the resulting roster are eligible to fill vacancies across the UN Secretariat for three years, though placement does not guarantee appointment.
Those offered positions receive a two-year fixed-term contract, with the possibility of a continuing contract subject to satisfactory performance.
Kenyans who are ineligible this cycle are encouraged to monitor future editions of the programme, as the participating country list is revised annually.
Alternative entry routes into the UN system include the UN Volunteers programme, junior professional officer schemes, internships, and mid-level vacancies open to all Member State nationals.

items.title: Saudi Arabia Reveals Jobs Kenyans Can Apply for Under New Labour Deal
items.description: Saudi Arabia clarifies Kenya labour annex covers only domestic workers and private drivers, while 293,600 job opportunities remain separate and unsigned.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!

Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development has clarified that the technical annex signed with Kenya on November 12, 2026, applies exclusively to domestic workers and private drivers.
The ministry confirmed the agreement does not cover skilled professionals in healthcare, construction, education, or any other sector.

The Saudi government urged the public to depend solely on its official channels for recruitment information, a move widely interpreted as a response to what it regards as inflated characterisations of the deal's scope.
The annex was signed in Riyadh by Deputy Minister of Human Resources and Social Development for Labour Abdullah Abuthnain and Cabinet Secretary Alfred Nganga Mutua.

It builds on a bilateral domestic worker recruitment agreement the two countries concluded on July 5, 2026.

The annex rests on three pillars: lowering recruitment costs, raising the quality of domestic workers through training and qualification programmes, and protecting the rights of all parties in the contractual relationship.
A separate letter of intent also established a three-month pilot programme on voluntary recruitment fees, designed to keep Kenya competitive against other labour-sending countries.

During and after his Riyadh visit, Mutua announced that Saudi employment agencies had committed to 293,600 job opportunities for Kenyans spanning healthcare, construction, hospitality, education, transport, manufacturing, finance, oil and gas, and domestic work.
He also said both governments had agreed that their technical teams would conclude a separate skilled workers recruitment framework within one month.
Those announcements described intentions and future negotiations rather than the contents of the signed document.
The Saudi clarification, issued on November 17, draws a firm distinction between the binding domestic worker annex and the broader discussions on skilled labour that remain unresolved.

No specific salary rates or a revised minimum wage for Kenyan workers have been agreed upon, and the promised skilled workers agreement has not yet been signed.
Notably, the 293,600 job commitments were made by recruitment agencies and private companies, not incorporated into the annex.
Without a signed skilled workers agreement, the framework needed to channel Kenyans into those professional roles does not yet exist.
For Kenyans in domestic work and private driving, the annex represents a tangible improvement: streamlined recruitment procedures, reduced costs, and stronger contractual protections.
Pre-departure training programmes are also set to be strengthened to better prepare workers before they depart.
For those seeking professional roles, the Saudi government has confirmed no agreement is currently in place.
Kenyans who have been approached with offers of skilled employment in Saudi Arabia before a formal framework is concluded should treat such offers with caution.

Mutua separately noted that Kenya had engaged Saudi authorities regarding travel restrictions linked to reported Ebola cases, stating that the case had been identified and isolated with no community transmission recorded.

items.title: CBK Governor Backs Treasury Plan to Centralise County Bank Accounts
items.description: Thugge said the proposals would improve government oversight of public funds, reduce the proliferation of commercial bank accounts and lower borrowing costs by allowing the National Treasury to access idle public resources.
content: NAIROBI, Kenya Nov 18 – Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) Governor Kamau Thugge has backed proposed amendments to the Public Finance Management Act seeking to centralise county government deposits at the Central Bank.

Appearing before the Senate Standing Committee on Finance and Budget, chaired by Ali Roba, Thugge supported proposals requiring county governments to obtain prior written approval from the National Treasury before opening or closing bank accounts.
The amendments also seek to consolidate county funds into a Treasury Single Account (TSA) at the CBK.

Thugge said the proposals would improve government oversight of public funds, reduce the proliferation of commercial bank accounts and lower borrowing costs by allowing the National Treasury to access idle public resources.

“We fully support this proposed amendment,” Thugge told senators, arguing that keeping county deposits at the Central Bank would eliminate unnecessary interest payments where government resources are already available.

items.title: Rapper Lil Maina joins Skye The Presence on remix ahead of album release
items.description: Kenyan rapper Lil Maina, one of the country’s most prominent contemporary music artists, joins forces with Skye The Presence on “Margiela Steppin (Remix)”, out November 13. The collaboration forms part of Maina’s forthcoming album, ‘Genge Rockstar’, a project that draws on the foundations of Genge and Kapuka while exploring their place within contemporary Kenyan music.- […]
content: Kenyan rapper Lil Maina, one of the country’s most prominent contemporary music artists, joins forces with Skye The Presence on “Margiela Steppin (Remix)”, out November 13.
The collaboration forms part of Maina’s forthcoming album, ‘Genge Rockstar’, a project that draws on the foundations of Genge and Kapuka while exploring their place within contemporary Kenyan music.

With an established presence in Kenya’s entertainment industry and a catalogue shaped by experimentation, Lil Maina has become an influential voice in a generation of artists redefining the country’s urban sound.

His latest collaboration with Skye The Presence reflects that approach, bringing together distinct creative perspectives while placing Sheng and contemporary Kenyan hip-hop at the centre of the release.

The release brings a new chapter to a track that first caught Maina’s attention when Skye The Presence shared a preview on social media, and now finds its way onto Lil Maina’s forthcoming album, ‘Genge Rockstar’.
For Maina, the collaboration began with a genuine appreciation for Skye The Presence’s approach to music.
He was drawn to the original snippet, particularly the way Skye brings Sheng into trap production.
When the original track was released on September 19, Lil Maina was already looking forward to hearing the full record.
The opportunity to revisit it came when his creative director, Philip Koth, told him that SKYE wanted to work on a remix. Lil Maina was immediately open to the idea.
“I like how he puts Sheng on trap beats. His approach is different. He is not afraid to express himself or do things his own way. He is free. He is art,” says Lil Maina.
The collaboration arrives at a time when Lil Maina is exploring a broader creative identity through his new album.

It takes its name from the meeting of two ideas that have shaped him: Genge and Kapuka, the Kenyan sounds he grew up listening to, and the Rockstar attitude that reflects how he sees himself today: expressive, experimental and unwilling to be confined to one version of his artistry. Rather than treating the past as something to recreate, Lil Maina is interested in carrying its energy into the present.
His approach has been to make music that can connect with listeners who remember the early 2000s while introducing those sounds to younger audiences encountering them from a different perspective.
“One generation is discovering something while another is reliving something,” he explains of the album’s relationship with nostalgia.
That interest in musical freedom also informs his decision to include “Margiela Steppin (Remix)” on the project.

Lil Maina sees the track as a natural fit for his current creative direction and the energy behind his Rockstar identity. It also reflects his willingness to move between sounds and collaborate with artists whose approaches challenge familiar expectations.
The release builds on a career that has seen Lil Maina move from online entertainment into a growing music catalogue.

Since his breakout single “Kishash” and his 2023 debut album, ‘Maisha Ya Stunna’, he has continued to explore different sides of his sound, drawing from Genge, hip-hop, dancehall and more melodic approaches.
His recent releases, including “Vimajor” and “Tetemesha”, have further explored the influence of early 2000s Kenyan music through a contemporary lens.

For Lil Maina, that evolution is also tied to how Kenyan music is received beyond the country. He believes local language and cultural identity should remain central to the music, rather than being altered to make it more accessible to international audiences.
Sheng, in particular, is an important part of the sound and expression he wants to carry forward.
His ambition is for listeners outside Kenya to connect with the music on its own terms, even when they do not understand every word.

items.title: Esri Eastern Africa Appoints Faith Nkatha Gitonga As CEO
items.description: Esri Eastern Africa has appointed Faith Nkatha Gitonga, who most recently worked at the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (TBI), as its new CEO
content: Esri Eastern Africa has appointed Faith Nkatha Gitonga, a technology and digital transformation leader who most recently worked at the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change (TBI), as its new Chief Executive Officer. She takes over leadership of the regional business on December 1, 2026.

Gitonga joins from TBI, where she served as interim Kenya country director and head of technology and digital transformation for Africa Advisory until April 2026. In that role, she worked on technology-driven reform in the public sector, experience that is directly relevant as governments across the region turn to geospatial intelligence, location analytics and digital mapping to plan infrastructure, manage resources, deliver services and make strategic decisions.

Before TBI, Gitonga led Cellulant’s Kenyan operations as country manager from 2020 to 2023, running one of the country’s prominent fintech businesses. Earlier in her career, she headed Oracle’s digital transformation business for Kenya’s public sector and held senior strategy and banking roles at Sidian Bank and Chase Bank. In all, she brings more than 15 years of leadership experience across financial services, payments, technology and public-sector transformation.
She also brings governance experience from the boards of Capital A Investment Bank, TechnoServe, PAL Network and LVCT Health, spanning business, development and corporate governance.

Esri Eastern Africa distributes geographic information systems (GIS) technology, including the ArcGIS platform, alongside spatial analytics, mapping, consulting and training services. Headquartered in Nairobi, it serves customers in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Ethiopia.

items.title: KENYA–INDIA DEFENCE PARTNERSHIP BRINGS SPECIALISED HEALTHCARE CLOSER TO COMMUNITIES
items.description: KENYA–INDIA DEFENCE PARTNERSHIP BRINGS SPECIALISED HEALTHCARE CLOSER TO COMMUNITIES Ministry of Defence – Kenya
content: Access to specialised healthcare remains a challenge for many underserved communities, particularly in remote areas where medical infrastructure and specialist services are limited. Through bilateral defence cooperation, the Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) and the Indian Armed Forces are combining their medical expertise and capabilities to expand access to essential healthcare services while advancing military medical collaboration.

Preparations for a joint Kenya–India medical outreach scheduled for early 2027 have gained momentum following reconnaissance and assessment visits by an Indian Armed Forces delegation to the Defence Forces Memorial Hospital (DFMH) in Nairobi and Chemolingot Sub-County Hospital in Tiaty Central, Baringo County.

The delegation, led by Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra and Colonel Debashirsh Paul, assessed DFMH’s medical facilities, infrastructure and operational preparedness to support the planned ophthalmic surgical outreach. The engagement focused on identifying medical, technical and logistical requirements necessary for the successful implementation of the programme.

In Baringo County, the delegation, which also included Captain Arjit Pande and was accompanied by Brigadier D. Chesiror from DFMH, was received by the Operation Maliza Uhalifu (OMU) Brigade Commander, Brigadier Ahmed Saman.

The team conducted a comprehensive assessment of Chemolingot Sub-County Hospital to establish its suitability for hosting the medical camp, evaluate existing healthcare capacity and identify the resources and logistical arrangements required to deliver specialised ophthalmic surgical procedures and general medical consultations.

The planned outreach will provide free medical services, with particular emphasis on specialised eye surgeries and general healthcare, targeting communities with limited access to such services. Beyond direct medical assistance, the initiative will facilitate professional knowledge exchange, skills development and collaboration between medical personnel from the two armed forces.

As part of the preparatory engagements, the delegation also paid a courtesy visit to the Deputy County Commissioner for Tiaty Central, Mr Justus Motanya, to enhance coordination with the local administration and facilitate community participation in the planned outreach.

The joint initiative demonstrates the growing significance of defence diplomacy in addressing humanitarian and community development needs. By integrating military medical expertise, institutional partnerships and local coordination, Kenya and India are translating bilateral defence cooperation into practical healthcare interventions that directly benefit communities.
The programme also reflects KDF’s broader commitment to civil-military cooperation, community welfare and the use of military capabilities to complement national healthcare efforts.

Through this partnership, the two armed forces seek to improve access to specialised treatment, promote medical knowledge exchange and deliver lasting humanitarian value, reinforcing the role of defence cooperation in advancing community health and well-being.

items.description: A new report flags gaps in mental health support in Kenyan schools, with many adolescents showing signs of depression and anxiety and counselling stretched

Mental health challenges among school-going children can affect concentration, classroom participation, relationships with peers and academic performance if left unaddressed. Learners experiencing anxiety and depression may also struggle with school attendance, social interactions and their ability to cope with academic demands.
